monument_name: Nārāyaṇa Mandira (believed to built during the Licchavi Period)
description_en: The Nārāyaṇa Mandira stands south of the road from Mangal Bazaar to Sundhārā. With a one-tier roof ofjhĩgaṭītiles, the temple faces west.A metal finial tops the roof with threepatāḥs made of brass hanging down from the finial to the eaves of the roof. The family members of Lakṣmī Bahādura Sinyā offered thepatāḥsto the deity in his memory in VS 2077 (2020 CE). The struts supporting the roof contain carvings of various forms of Nārāyaṇa. An image of Nārayaṇa flanked by Goddesses Lakṃī and Sarasvatī is depicted on the woodentoraṇasurmounting the main entrance to the sanctum. The originaltoraṇawas stolen long ago and was replaced by a new one after the reconstruction of the Temple. A stone figure of lion is placed on either side of the staircase that lead to the main entrance, and a stone statue of Nārāyaṇa flanked by Lakṣmī and Sarasvatī atop of ajalaharīis enshrined in the sanctum. Two right hands of Nārāyaṇa carry a mace (gadā)and lotus (padma) while his two left hands carry a conch shell (śaṅkha)and wheel (cakra).Locals date this temple back to the Licchavi period, however, there are no historical sources to support that. It suffered damages during the 2015 earthquakes, and was rebuilt afterward with the grant assistance of 700,000 rupees from the Lalitpur Municipality and donations of 500,000 rupees that were collected from local donors. The old set of the doorframe of the main entrance to the sanctum was used again in the reconstruction. The inauguration of the temple is yet to take place, as some works of the plinth are yet to complete (as of July 2021).The temple neither has a priest nor does any socio-religious event takes place here. Locals, in the course of making rounds to various shrines early morning, worship the main deity of this temple as well.
description_ne: ललितपुरको मङ्गलबजारबाट सुन्धारा जाँदा सुन्धारा अलिकति नपुग्दै बाटोको दक्षिणमा यो मन्दिर अवस्थित छ । एक तह झिंगटीको छाना रहेको यो मन्दिर पश्चिमाभिमुख गरी बनाइएको छ । मन्दिरको छानामा धातुको गजूर राखिएको छ । गजूरदेखि छानासम्म पुने गरी पित्तलका तीनवटा पता: चढाइएका छन् । विसं २०७७ (सन् २०२०) मा लक्ष्मीबहादुर सिन्याको स्मृतिमा परिवारका सदस्यहरूले पता: चढाएका थिए । छानाको भार थाम्न राखिएका टुँडालमा नारायणका विभिन्न रूप कुँदिएका छन् । मन्दिरको गर्भगृहभित्र प्रवेश गर्ने कलात्मक ढोकामाथि नारायण, लक्ष्मी र सरस्वती अंकित काष्ठ तोरण राखिएको छ । धेरै वर्ष पहिले नै तोरण चोरी भइसकेको थियो । मन्दिर पुनर्निर्माण गरेपछि अहिले नयाँ तोरण राखिएको हो । मन्दिरको गर्भगृहमा जाने सिँढीको दायाँबायाँ राखिएको सिंह पुरानो देखिन्छ । गर्भगृहभित्र जलहरिमाथि नारायणको ढुङ्गाको मूर्ति स्थापना गरिएको छ । नारायणले दायाँ दुई हातमा गदा र पद्म लिएका छन् भने बायाँ दुई हातमा शङ्ख र चक्र समातेका छन् । नारायणको दायाँबायाँ लक्ष्मी र सरस्वती पनि राखिएको छन् ।स्थानीयहरू यस मन्दिरलाई लिच्छविलीन मान्छन् तर मन्दिरको प्राचीनताबारे जानकारी कुनै अभिलेख प्राप्त भएको छैन । सन् १९७० मा मन्दिरको जीर्णोद्धार गरिएको थियो । विसं २०७२ (सन् २०१५) को भूकम्पले मन्दिर चर्किएको थियो । ललितपुर महानगरपालिकाबाट प्राप्त रु. ७ लाख र चन्दाबाट जम्मा भएको ५ लाख गरी जम्मा ११ लाख खर्च गरी मन्दिरको पुनर्निर्माण गरिएको छ । पुनर्निर्माण गर्दा प्रवेशद्वार चाहिँ पुरानै प्रयोग गरिएको छ । मन्दिरको पुनर्निर्माण कार्य सकिए पनि पेटीको काम बाँकी भएकोले औपचारिक रूपमा उद्घाटन गरिएको छैन ।यस मन्दिरमा कुनै पूजारी नियुक्त गरिएको छैन र कुनै धार्मिक सांस्कृतिक गतिविधि पनि गरिँदैन । स्थानीयहरू बिहान उठेेर अन्य देवताहरूको पूजा गर्ने क्रममा यस मन्दिरमा पनि पूजा गर्ने गर्छन् ।

historical_events.event_description: Pruscha1975 (P-250) mentions that it  was renovated in 1970.
The Temple suffered damages during the 2015 earthquakes.
Prākāśa Sinyā offered the bell to the Temple in the memory of his father Rāmalāla Sinyā and mother Julumanānī Sinyā.

After it suffered damages during the 2015 earthquakes, it was rebuilt with the grant assistance of 700,000 rupees from the Lalitpur Metropolis and donations of 500,000 rupees from the locals. The old set of the doorframe of the main entrance to the sanctum was used again in the reconstruction. The inauguration of the Temple is yet to take place, as some works of the plinth are yet to complete (as of July 2021).
Thepatāḥwas offered by Madanadevī Sinyā together with her sons Maheśvara and Rabina in the memory of her husband/their father Lakṣmī Bahādura Sinyā.
